title: Asbestos regulated areas and exposure monitoring practice questions
description: Practice questions on OSHA asbestos regulated areas and exposure monitoring: access, assessments, daily monitoring, notice (29 CFR 1926.1101(e)-(f)).

questions.question: A crew will do Class III asbestos work, and the employer expects airborne levels to stay low. Under 1926.1101(e)(1), where must the work be conducted?

options.A: Within a regulated area only if airborne concentrations are shown to exceed a PEL
options.B: Within a regulated area
options.C: Within a regulated area only if the material is friable
options.D: Anywhere on the site, as long as a competent person is present

questions.explanation: Paragraph (e)(1) states: "All Class I, II and III asbestos work shall be conducted within regulated areas." The PEL-based condition applies only to "All other operations covered by this standard."
questions.evidence: All Class I, II and III asbestos work shall be conducted within regulated areas.

questions.question: An operation is covered by the asbestos standard but is not Class I, II or III work. Under 1926.1101(e)(1), when must it be conducted within a regulated area?

options.A: Only after a laboratory confirms the material contains asbestos
options.B: Only when the work lasts longer than one full shift
options.C: Only when more than one employer is working on the site
options.D: Where airborne concentrations of asbestos exceed, or there is a reasonable possibility they may exceed, a PEL

questions.explanation: Other covered operations "shall be conducted within a regulated area where airborne concentrations of asbestos exceed, or there is a reasonable possibility they may exceed a PEL."
questions.evidence: All other operations covered by this standard shall be conducted within a regulated area where airborne concentrations of asbestos exceed, or there is a reasonable possibility they may exceed a PEL.

questions.topic: Demarcation, access and conduct in regulated areas
questions.question: Under 1926.1101(e)(2), what must the manner of demarcating a regulated area achieve?

options.A: It minimizes the number of persons within the area and protects persons outside the area from exposure to airborne asbestos
options.B: It uses solid walls on every side of the area
options.C: It keeps the area no larger than the room where the work takes place
options.D: It is approved in writing by the building owner before work starts

questions.explanation: The regulated area "shall be demarcated in any manner that minimizes the number of persons within the area and protects persons outside the area from exposure to airborne asbestos."
questions.evidence: The regulated area shall be demarcated in any manner that minimizes the number of persons within the area and protects persons outside the area from exposure to airborne asbestos.

questions.topic: Demarcation, access and conduct in regulated areas
questions.question: Under 1926.1101(e)(3), to whom is access to a regulated area limited?

options.A: Any employee of any contractor working on the project
options.B: Any person who is wearing a respirator
options.C: Authorized persons and persons authorized by the Act or regulations issued pursuant thereto
options.D: The competent person only

questions.explanation: Paragraph (e)(3) states: "Access to regulated areas shall be limited to authorized persons and to persons authorized by the Act or regulations issued pursuant thereto."
questions.evidence: Access to regulated areas shall be limited to authorized persons and to persons authorized by the Act or regulations issued pursuant thereto.

questions.topic: Demarcation, access and conduct in regulated areas
questions.question: Employees in a regulated area are required by paragraph (h)(1) to wear respirators. An authorized person who is not on the crew needs to enter. What does 1926.1101(e)(4) require?

options.A: The person shall be supplied with a respirator selected in accordance with paragraph (h)(3)
options.B: The person may enter without a respirator if the visit is short
options.C: The person must provide a respirator of their own choosing
options.D: The person must wait outside until the work is finished

questions.explanation: "All persons entering a regulated area where employees are required pursuant to paragraph (h)(1) of this section to wear respirators shall be supplied with a respirator selected in accordance with paragraph (h)(3) of this section."
questions.evidence: All persons entering a regulated area where employees are required pursuant to paragraph (h)(1) of this section to wear respirators shall be supplied with a respirator selected in accordance with paragraph (h)(3) of this section.

questions.topic: Demarcation, access and conduct in regulated areas
questions.question: Under 1926.1101(e)(5), which activities must the employer ensure employees do not do in the regulated area?

options.A: Smoke only; eating and drinking are allowed during breaks
options.B: Eat, drink, smoke, chew tobacco or gum, or apply cosmetics
options.C: Use portable electric tools or extension cords
options.D: Use phones or two-way radios

questions.explanation: "The employer shall ensure that employees do not eat, drink, smoke, chew tobacco or gum, or apply cosmetics in the regulated area."
questions.evidence: The employer shall ensure that employees do not eat, drink, smoke, chew tobacco or gum, or apply cosmetics in the regulated area.

questions.topic: Demarcation, access and conduct in regulated areas
questions.question: Under 1926.1101(e)(6), who must supervise all asbestos work performed within regulated areas?

options.A: The building owner or the owner's representative
options.B: A licensed physician
options.C: An inspector from the State environmental agency
options.D: A competent person, as defined in paragraph (b)

questions.explanation: "The employer shall ensure that all asbestos work performed within regulated areas is supervised by a competent person, as defined in paragraph (b) of this section."
questions.evidence: The employer shall ensure that all asbestos work performed within regulated areas is supervised by a competent person, as defined in paragraph (b) of this section.

questions.question: Under 1926.1101(f)(1)(ii), what must determinations of employee exposure be made from?

options.A: Bulk samples of the material being disturbed
options.B: Area samples taken only at the edge of the regulated area
options.C: Breathing zone air samples representative of the 8-hour TWA and 30-minute short-term exposures of each employee
options.D: Samples taken only on the competent person

questions.explanation: "Determinations of employee exposure shall be made from breathing zone air samples that are representative of the 8-hour TWA and 30-minute short-term exposures of each employee."
questions.evidence: Determinations of employee exposure shall be made from breathing zone air samples that are representative of the 8-hour TWA and 30-minute short-term exposures of each employee.

questions.question: Under 1926.1101(f)(1)(iii), representative 30-minute short-term exposures are based on samples representing 30-minute exposures associated with which operations?

options.A: The first 30 minutes of each shift, whatever the task
options.B: Operations chosen at random during the shift
options.C: Operations that produce the lowest exposures in the work area
options.D: Operations that are most likely to produce exposures above the excursion limit

questions.explanation: Short-term exposures are based on samples "representing 30 minute exposures associated with operations that are most likely to produce exposures above the excursion limit for employees in each work area."
questions.evidence: Representative 30-minute short-term employee exposures shall be determined on the basis of one or more samples representing 30 minute exposures associated with operations that are most likely to produce exposures above the excursion limit for employees in each work area.

questions.question: Under 1926.1101(f)(2)(i), who conducts the initial exposure assessment, and when?

options.A: A competent person, immediately before or at the initiation of the operation
options.B: An accredited laboratory, after the first week of work
options.C: The building owner, before the contract is awarded
options.D: Any employee on the crew, at the end of the first shift

questions.explanation: The employer "shall ensure that a “competent person” conducts an exposure assessment immediately before or at the initiation of the operation to ascertain expected exposures during that operation or workplace."
questions.evidence: Each employer who has a workplace or work operation covered by this standard shall ensure that a “competent person” conducts an exposure assessment immediately before or at the initiation of the operation to ascertain expected exposures during that operation or workplace.

questions.question: Under 1926.1101(f)(2)(ii), what must the initial exposure assessment take into consideration?

options.A: The monitoring results from the current job, and nothing else
options.B: Only the product label of the material to be disturbed
options.C: Both the monitoring results and all observations, information or calculations which indicate employee exposure to asbestos
options.D: Only the number of employees assigned to the job

questions.explanation: "The assessment shall take into consideration both the monitoring results and all observations, information or calculations which indicate employee exposure to asbestos, including any previous monitoring conducted in the workplace".
questions.evidence: The assessment shall take into consideration both the monitoring results and all observations, information or calculations which indicate employee exposure to asbestos, including any previous monitoring conducted in the workplace,

questions.question: A Class I job is starting. The employer has not yet conducted exposure monitoring for it and has not made a negative exposure assessment. Under 1926.1101(f)(2)(ii), what shall the employer presume?

options.A: That employees are exposed below the PELs until monitoring shows otherwise
options.B: That employees are exposed in excess of the TWA and excursion limit
options.C: That employees are exposed in excess of the TWA, but not of the excursion limit
options.D: That employees are exposed in excess of the excursion limit, but not of the TWA

questions.explanation: For Class I asbestos work, until the employer documents otherwise or makes a negative exposure assessment, "the employer shall presume that employees are exposed in excess of the TWA and excursion limit."
questions.evidence: the employer shall presume that employees are exposed in excess of the TWA and excursion limit.

questions.question: Under 1926.1101(f)(2)(iii), what may a negative exposure assessment be made for?

options.A: Any one specific asbestos job which will be performed by employees who have been trained in compliance with the standard
options.B: All of the employer's asbestos jobs for the next 12 months
options.C: Any asbestos job, whether or not the employees have been trained
options.D: A whole building, covering every contractor working in it

questions.explanation: The rule reads: "For any one specific asbestos job which will be performed by employees who have been trained in compliance with the standard, the employer may demonstrate that employee exposures will be below the PELs".
questions.evidence: For any one specific asbestos job which will be performed by employees who have been trained in compliance with the standard, the employer may demonstrate that employee exposures will be below the PELs

questions.question: An employer wants to use objective data under 1926.1101(f)(2)(iii)(A). The data must show the material or activity cannot release airborne fibers above the TWA and excursion limit under which work conditions?

options.A: Average work conditions over a typical week
options.B: The conditions inside the manufacturer's test laboratory only
options.C: The conditions expected on the first day of the job only
options.D: Those work conditions having the greatest potential for releasing asbestos

questions.explanation: Objective data must show the material or activity "cannot release airborne fibers in concentrations exceeding the TWA and excursion limit under those work conditions having the greatest potential for releasing asbestos".
questions.evidence: cannot release airborne fibers in concentrations exceeding the TWA and excursion limit under those work conditions having the greatest potential for releasing asbestos

questions.question: An employer relies on monitoring data from prior asbestos jobs under 1926.1101(f)(2)(iii)(B). How must the training and experience of the employees on those prior jobs compare with the current crew's?

options.A: At least as extensive as that of employees performing the current job
options.B: No more extensive than that of employees performing the current job
options.C: More extensive than that of employees performing the current job
options.D: Any level, because training and experience are not considered for prior-job data

questions.explanation: Paragraph (f)(2)(iii)(B) requires that "the operations were conducted by employees whose training and experience are no more extensive than that of employees performing the current job".
questions.evidence: the operations were conducted by employees whose training and experience are no more extensive than that of employees performing the current job,

questions.question: Employees are assigned to work within a regulated area doing Class II work. No negative exposure assessment has been made for the entire operation, and they do not all wear supplied-air respirators in a positive pressure mode. What monitoring does 1926.1101(f)(3)(i) require?

options.A: Monitoring at intervals sufficient to document the validity of the exposure prediction
options.B: Monitoring once at the start of the job and once at the end
options.C: Daily monitoring that is representative of the exposure of each employee
options.D: Monitoring of one employee per crew each week

questions.explanation: "The employer shall conduct daily monitoring that is representative of the exposure of each employee who is assigned to work within a regulated area who is performing Class I or II work". The "intervals sufficient" wording applies to operations other than Class I and II.
questions.evidence: The employer shall conduct daily monitoring that is representative of the exposure of each employee who is assigned to work within a regulated area who is performing Class I or II work,

questions.question: A Class I crew uses a modification of a control method listed in (g)(4)(i), and all of them wear supplied-air respirators operated in the pressure demand mode. Under 1926.1101(f)(3)(iii), what monitoring applies to them?

options.A: Daily monitoring may be dispensed with because of the respirators
options.B: They are monitored only when a change in work practices occurs
options.C: They shall continue to be monitored daily
options.D: They are monitored once a week instead of daily

questions.explanation: The exception for supplied-air respirators does not cover them: employees doing Class I work "using a modification of a listed control method, shall continue to be monitored daily even if they are equipped with supplied-air respirators."
questions.evidence: using a modification of a listed control method, shall continue to be monitored daily even if they are equipped with supplied-air respirators.

questions.question: A negative exposure assessment was produced for a specific job. Midway through, the employer changes personnel in a way that may result in new exposures above the permissible exposure limit. What does 1926.1101(f)(4)(ii) require?

options.A: Institute the exposure monitoring required under paragraph (f)(3)
options.B: Nothing new, because the negative exposure assessment stays valid for that job
options.C: Stop the job until a new negative exposure assessment is approved by OSHA
options.D: Monitor only the new employees, once, at the end of the job

questions.explanation: The employer "shall institute the exposure monitoring required under paragraph (f)(3) of this section whenever there has been a change in process, control equipment, personnel or work practices" that may raise exposures, and it is required "regardless of whether a “negative exposure assessment” was previously produced for a specific job."
questions.evidence: Such additional monitoring is required regardless of whether a “negative exposure assessment” was previously produced for a specific job.

questions.question: What deadline does 1926.1101(f)(5) set for notifying each affected employee of monitoring results?

options.A: No later than 15 working days after the receipt of the results
options.B: No later than 30 calendar days after the job ends
options.C: At the end of the project, together with the final report
options.D: As soon as possible but no later than 5 working days after the receipt of the results

questions.explanation: "The employer must, as soon as possible but no later than 5 working days after the receipt of the results of any monitoring performed under this section, notify each affected employee of these results".
questions.evidence: The employer must, as soon as possible but no later than 5 working days after the receipt of the results of any monitoring performed under this section, notify each affected employee of these results

questions.question: An employees' designated representative will observe exposure monitoring inside an area where protective clothing and equipment are required. Under 1926.1101(f)(6)(ii), what applies to the observer?

options.A: The observer must watch from outside the area only
options.B: The observer shall be provided with and be required to use such clothing and equipment
options.C: The observer must bring their own clothing and equipment
options.D: The observer may enter without protective clothing if not touching any material

questions.explanation: When observation requires entry into such an area, "the observer shall be provided with and be required to use such clothing and equipment and shall comply with all other applicable safety and health procedures."
questions.evidence: the observer shall be provided with and be required to use such clothing and equipment
